findings.title: A draft commit finishing while public identity is revoked still loses its committed CAS version
findings.evidence: enqueue captures authorized namespace N and version 0, saveDraft commits version 1 while logout/offline/401 revokes authority. App recoveryHost.namespace() then returns null because ConnectionSession.authorized(N) is false. Post-commit update requires a non-null identity, so state.version remains 0; current() rejects, but durable draft is already version 1. Reauth of the same retained workspace and explicit retry uses stale expectedVersion 0 and repeatedly conflicts. Current same-namespace reauth test increments generation while namespace remains available and does not model this interval.
findings.impact: Explicit retry/saving can remain blocked after a valid reconnect, despite the original draft commit having succeeded. No data overwrite or automatic POST is claimed.
findings.requested: Retain successful version knowledge scoped to the captured workspace/namespace/view even during temporary auth loss; do not revive authorization or resume the old command. Add controlled commit-held -> public namespace null/auth false -> commit completes -> same namespace reauth -> explicit save/retry case, while cross-namespace case remains isolated.
